reply: This is the demo, so nobody reads your message. In a real run the agent attached to the run reads it within seconds and answers here: ask it why it recommends something, ask it to look again at a finding, or attach a cited paper it could not fetch. A message never changes the run by itself; only the decision buttons do.

steps.title: Welcome: how a paper starts
steps.body:
This page shows your toolkit and follows every paper you verify. You start a paper from your agent, not from here: open a terminal in the PaperFormalizer folder, start claude or codex, and ask it as in this box (copy gives you the words).

The agent starts the run, attaches itself to it and acts at every halt; the run then appears on this page and updates live.

For this demo a paper has already been started. Press Next.

steps.title: Your papers
steps.body:
Every paper you verify is a row here, with its stage and whether it waits for you; Needs you at the top counts what does.

Here is the demo's paper, Two Elementary Inequalities, made up for this tour. One of its theorems is stated too broadly, on purpose, so you can see what happens then.

Click its row, or press Next.

steps.title: The paper's page
steps.body:
This is where you follow one paper. On the left: the run's stages, and a proof map (an arrow reads "used by"). In the middle: the paper itself. On the right: PaperFormalizer's comments.

An agent session (Claude Code or Codex) is attached to the run. It acts at every halt and talks with you here. In this demo a stand-in plays it.

Press Next to let the referee read the paper.

steps.title: A repair that would weaken a main result
steps.body:
The referee found that Theorem 3 is false as printed: for a = b = −1 the left side is −1 and the right side is 1. The only true version adds a, b ≥ 0, which claims less than the paper does.

That is your decision, never the agent's. The printed text is marked red, the proposed statement blue, and the card in the margin holds the agent's recommendation.

Choose Accept, Redo with guidance or Decline on the card and press Send my decisions, or press Accept all recommendations in the box under the title.

events.message: referee: grading 4 results for faithfulness, ambiguity and correctness
fixer: no repair keeps Theorem 3 at full strength — suggesting the strongest true version

steps.title: Promotion round A: cited results
steps.body:
Your decision went to the run: the referee confirmed the repaired Theorem 3, and the Lean plan was made.

The paper uses Schur's inequality without proving it, citing a book. Round A offers to build it in your toolkit, so this paper and later ones can use it instead of assuming it.

The checklist is at the end of the paper, with the agent's recommendation. Decide the entry, or press Accept all recommendations, and apply the round.

events.message: confirming the accepted repair of Theorem 3
round A: looking for the cited results in Mathlib and your toolkit

steps.title: Promotion round B: the paper's results
steps.body:
The Lean stages proved the paper's results and the report is written. Round B offers the proved results to your toolkit.

Here the agent recommends accepting the cubic inequality, which is new, and declining the AM-GM inequality, because Mathlib already has it. You may follow it or not, entry by entry.

Decide, then apply round B.

events.message: round A: building Schur's inequality in your toolkit
F5: each statement linked to the paper's words
writing the report and the corrected paper

steps.title: The result
steps.body:
The run is finished. The top of the page gives the verdict: an error was found and repaired. Use the Markup switch above the paper to read it as corrected or as printed.

Click a result to open its drawer: the referee's verdict, the conditions added, and its Lean statement linked to the paper's words.

events.message: round B: the accepted result enters your toolkit

steps.title: Talking to the agent
steps.body:
You can write to the agent at any time with Message the agent, and attach files (a cited paper, say). Its answers appear under yours. Try it: the stand-in answers.

When the agent needs something only you can give, its request shows here and under Needs you.

steps.title: Your library
steps.body: The Library lists your toolkit's results, read from its Lean files: Schur's inequality from round A and the cubic inequality from round B are now there, each with its statement and what uses it.

steps.title: That is the tour
steps.body:
To verify a paper of your own, ask your agent, for example: "Use PaperFormalizer to verify arXiv 2401.01234 with my toolkit at ~/my-toolkit." It starts the run, brings up this page and gives you the link.

To let the agent take your decisions too (each listed for your review afterwards), have it start the run with --full-auto.

Press Start over to see the tour again.
